summary.hospital_course: The patient is a 79-year-old female readmitted 9 days post-discharge with recurrent volume overload, presenting with an admission weight of 75.8 kg against a documented dry weight of 71.4 kg. She was diuresed with intravenous furosemide to a discharge weight of 71.9 kg. Sacubitril-valsartan was uptitrated to 49/51 mg twice daily and low-dose spironolactone was added. Potassium (4.1 mEq/L) and creatinine (1.4 mg/dL) remained stable at discharge. Medication review noted intermittent adherence to furosemide due to memory issues; a dosette box and home scales were provided. Physiotherapy signed off, though the patient remains short of breath on minimal exertion and uses a rolling walker. She lives alone without caregiver support or transport arrangements. Daughter was notified by phone. Teach-back on spironolactone was incomplete and needs repetition prior to departure. A basic metabolic panel is required within 5 days post-discharge.
summary.condition_at_discharge: Short of breath on minimal exertion, ambulating with a rolling walker. Weight 71.9 kg, potassium 4.1 mEq/L, creatinine 1.4 mg/dL. Physiotherapy signed off; spironolactone teach-back incomplete.

interactions.description: Loop diuretics can reduce renal clearance of metformin and raise its plasma concentration.
interactions.recommendation: Check renal function after any diuretic dose increase.

interactions.description: Additive hypotension, particularly during uptitration of either agent.
interactions.recommendation: Uptitrate one agent at a time and monitor blood pressure and symptoms.

interactions.description: Renin-angiotensin system blockade can reduce renal function, raising metformin accumulation and lactic-acidosis risk in chronic kidney disease.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor renal function; reduce the metformin dose if eGFR falls below 45.

interactions.description: Additive hyperkalaemia risk, amplified in chronic kidney disease.
interactions.recommendation: Check potassium and creatinine within 5-7 days and again at 4 weeks.

education.plain_language_summary: You were in the hospital because extra water built up in your body and made it hard for your heart to work. Your care team adjusted your heart and water medicines to remove extra fluid. At home, you will need to weigh yourself every morning, take your medicines using your pill organizer, and watch for warning signs like sudden weight gain or swelling.
medication_instructions: Furosemide 40 mg (water pill): Take 1 pill twice daily, once in the morning and once in the late afternoon. Dose increased from once daily to help remove extra fluid.
Sacubitril-valsartan 49/51 mg (heart pill): Take 1 pill twice daily, once in the morning and once in the evening. Dose increased to strengthen heart function.
Spironolactone 12.5 mg (heart and water pill): Take 1 pill once daily in the morning. This is a NEW medicine started for heart protection.
Metoprolol succinate 25 mg (heart rate pill): Take 1 pill once daily in the morning. Continued unchanged.
Apixaban 5 mg (blood thinner): Take 1 pill twice daily, once in the morning and once in the evening. Continued unchanged.
Metformin 500 mg (blood sugar pill): Take 1 pill twice daily with meals in the morning and evening. Continued unchanged.

How to use your pill organizer (dosette box): Fill your weekly pill organizer once a week. Put your morning medicines (Furosemide, Sacubitril-valsartan, Spironolactone, Metoprolol, Apixaban, Metformin) in the morning compartment. Put your evening medicines (Furosemide in late afternoon, Sacubitril-valsartan, Apixaban, Metformin) in the evening compartment. Using this organizer every day prevents missing doses of your water pill which caused fluid build-up in the past.
activity_and_diet: Weigh yourself every morning right after using the bathroom and before eating or drinking. Write down your weight on a chart daily.
Use your walker or walking aid every time you stand up or walk around your home to stay safe and prevent falls.
Follow a low-salt diet to keep extra water from building up in your body.
red_flag_symptoms: You gain more than 3 pounds in 1 day or more than 5 pounds in 1 week.
Your ankles, feet, legs, or belly swell or feel tighter.
You have new or worsening trouble breathing when walking, resting, or trying to sleep flat.
You feel dizzy, lightheaded, faint, or confused.
Chest pain or severe sudden shortness of breath (call 911 immediately).
